description: "This three-level meta-analysis of 41 studies (N = 8376) reveals that business decision-making games significantly enhance training effectiveness with a moderate overall effect (g = 0.53). The games effectively improve reactions (g = 0.44), learning processes (g = 0.66), and performance (g = 0.45), with the strongest impact on trainee motivation (g = 0.85). These positive outcomes remain robust across various participant types, game designs, and academic fields, supporting the broad implementation of such games in business education."
responsibilities: "I was responsible for developing the standardized workflow code for the meta-analysis."
